newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish '97 mobile phones sales seen at 600,000.
newsitem.headline: Finnish '97 mobile phones sales seen at 600,000.

text.p: Sales in Finland of new mobile phones are expected to increase to about 600,000 units this year from 500,000 delivered by importers and wholesalers to retail stores last year, the association of Finnish electronics wholesalers said in a statement on Friday.
In 1995, sales of new mobile phones in Finland totalled 384,000 units, the association said, noting this meant 1996 sales had increased 30 percent.
"This year, Finns are expected to buy about 600,000 mobile phones," it said. In October, the association forecast that 1997 sales would rise to 590,000 units from 495,000 expected in 1996.
Of wholesalers' 1996 new mobile phone deliveries to retailers, 443,000 were GSM-phones.
The value at consumer prices of total Finnish 1996 mobile phones sales was "slightly more than one billion markka," the association said.
In Sweden, sales of new mobile phones had exceeded 970,000 units by end-November, and so full-year 1996 sales in Sweden would rise above one million units, the association said.
